current_public.description:
Compare nearby Bluetooth Low Energy signal strength while searching for an accessory you own or have permission to locate. The accessory must be actively advertising and visible to your iPhone.

A CLEARER WAY TO SEARCH
Start with the in-app guide: wake your accessory, choose by Bluetooth name and advertised manufacturer, then move a few slow steps and wait for fresh readings. A stronger signal alone does not identify your item.

LIVE MAP AND SIGNAL LIST
See device names, advertised manufacturers, and measured RSSI. When these details are unavailable, clear unnamed-device and manufacturer-unavailable labels explain what is missing. Stronger signals sit nearer the map center. Expand, pan, zoom, or choose a signal from the list. Dot angles are visual spacing, not compass directions.

COMPARE WITH CONFIDENCE
Follow smoothed strength, recent readings, and warmer-or-colder trends. Clear freshness and paused/lost states distinguish a live reading from historical data. Reset the comparison for another position. Pause, resume, and return to the signal list with direct controls. Haptic feedback can be switched off.

FREE AND PRIVATE
All features are free, without an account, subscription, or time limit. Scanning and analysis happen on your phone. Names and manufacturer identifiers are processed in memory on your phone. There is no location tracking, analytics, advertising, or signal upload.

UNDERSTAND THE LIMITS
RSSI is approximate relative signal strength, not exact distance. Walls, reflections, orientation, and transmit power affect results. Headphones, earbuds, and other accessories may stop advertising while asleep, connected, or in a closed case. Silent and powered-off devices cannot appear. Signal Scout does not verify people, device owners, or broadcast identity and does not replace an accessory maker's finding network.

Support: https://nickvan23-lang.github.io/signal-scout/support.html
Privacy: https://nickvan23-lang.github.io/signal-scout/privacy.html

description.value:
Find your way toward a nearby Bluetooth Low Energy accessory by comparing its signal strength. Signal Scout helps you search for an item you own or have permission to locate, while it is powered on and actively advertising to your iPhone.

SEE WHAT IS NEARBY
Scan for BLE signals and see advertised device names, manufacturers, and measured signal strength (RSSI). Names and manufacturer information are clues, not verified identities. Some devices appear without these details.

COMPARE AS YOU MOVE
Choose a signal, take a few slow steps, and wait for fresh readings. Follow smoothed strength and warmer-or-colder trends. Clear paused, stale, and lost states help you distinguish current readings from historical data. Reset your comparison when you change position.

EXPLORE THE SIGNAL MAP
Stronger signals appear nearer the center. Expand, pan, zoom, or choose a device from the signal list. Dot angles provide visual spacing; they do not show compass direction.

PRIVATE AND SIMPLE
All features are available without an account, subscription, or time limit. Scanning and analysis happen on your iPhone. There is no location tracking, advertising, analytics, or signal upload. Optional haptic feedback can be switched off.

KNOW WHAT BLUETOOTH CAN TELL YOU
Signal strength is a relative clue, not exact distance. Walls, reflections, device orientation, and transmit power affect readings. A stronger signal alone does not identify your accessory.

Earbuds, headphones, speakers, and other accessories appear only when they advertise a compatible BLE signal. They may stop advertising while asleep, connected, or in a closed case. Silent and powered-off devices cannot appear.

Signal Scout does not provide GPS tracking, a finding network, or verified device ownership. It does not replace your accessory maker's finding service.

Requires an iPhone with iOS 17.0 or later and Bluetooth permission.

Support: https://nickvan23-lang.github.io/signal-scout/support.html
Privacy: https://nickvan23-lang.github.io/signal-scout/privacy.html
Terms: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/
